title: Let agents pick up routine tickets and fix failing checks
summary: The SuperPlane team says 52% of the code changes they merged last month came from their tool, which picks tickets, runs coding agents and fixes failing checks.
agent_role: The system scans the backlog, picks suitable tickets, runs a coding agent, verifies the result and handles failed checks and review comments. Humans review the evidence and decide what ships.
outcome: The team reports that 52% of the pull requests they merged last month were automated through SuperPlane.
what_they_did: The team behind Semaphore built SuperPlane, an open-source tool that coordinates coding agents. It scans the team's backlog for tickets suited to automation and runs a coding agent on them. It checks the result and works through failed automatic tests and review feedback. Engineers then review the evidence and decide what ships.
how_it_went: They say 52% of the code changes their team merged last month came through this system.
worth_knowing: This is the makers' own launch post, so the 52% figure is their claim about their own team.
prompt: Look through the open tickets in [project tracker] for [repo URL]. Pick up to [number] small, well-defined tickets suited to automation and explain why you chose each. For each one, make the change on a separate branch, run the automatic tests and fix any failures. Then open a draft change request with a summary of what you did and the test results. Do not merge anything; wait for my review.

curation.rationale: Mostly a product launch, but it reports a concrete in-house result (52% of merged changes automated) from an open-source tool. Evidence is the company's own claim.
